chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, who said: I heard Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) by a grave while he was saying:
Indeed, for something whose end is this, it is truly rightful that one is abstinent at its beginning, and indeed, for something whose beginning is this, it is truly rightful that one fears its end.

key_terms.يُخَافَ: To be feared or regarded with apprehension
key_terms.يُزْهَدَ: To be made unattractive or to abstain from due to lack of desire

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ethical principle regarding the relationship between the beginning and end of an action?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this narration highlights Imam Musa ibn Ja'far’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on *tadabbur* (contemplation of consequences) as a cornerstone of ethical decision-making. By invoking the grave as a tangible reminder of the ultimate return to Allah, the Imam teaches that the nature of the end (*al-akhirah*) should dictate one's attitude toward the beginning (*al-awwal*), encouraging proactive zeal for beneficial deeds and cautious restraint from those leading to ruin.
